name: TFR2-related hemochromatosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for hereditary hemochromatosis type 3

criteria.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in the TFR2 gene confirmed by genetic testing
Persistently elevated serum ferritin levels above normal reference range
Increased transferrin saturation >45% on at least two occasions
Exclusion of secondary causes of iron overload such as chronic liver disease or multiple transfusions
Presence of clinical features consistent with iron overload such as hepatomegaly or arthropathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic TFR2 variants plus elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation, with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Liver biopsy may be used to assess iron overload severity but is not mandatory if genetic and biochemical criteria are met.

common.symptomName: Arthropathy involving second and third metacarpophalangeal joints
searchTerms: arthritis in second and third finger joints

common.symptomName: Elevated serum transaminases indicating liver injury
searchTerms: high liver enzymes indicating liver damage
heart muscle disease with irregular heartbeat

occasional.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to pancreatic iron deposition
searchTerms: blood sugar problems due to iron buildup
low sex drive from low gonadal hormones
reduced sexual desire due to hormone deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Elevated serum ferritin without clinical symptoms
searchTerms: raised ferritin with no clinical signs

occasional.symptomName: Mild hepatocellular carcinoma risk in advanced disease
searchTerms: increased liver cancer risk in late disease
hepatocellular carcinoma risk in advanced stage

rare.symptomName: Congestive heart failure due to iron cardiomyopathy
searchTerms: heart failure from iron heart disease
fluid buildup due to iron cardiomyopathy
weak heart pumping from iron overload
low thyroid hormone from iron overload

imaging: Echocardiogram showing cardiomyopathy in advanced cases
other: Liver biopsy demonstrating increased hepatic iron concentration (optional)

distinguishingFeatures: Typically later onset than TFR2-related hemochromatosis
More common in Northern European populations
Mutations in HJV or HAMP genes
More severe clinical presentation with cardiac failure

redFlags: Rapidly progressive liver fibrosis or cirrhosis
Unexplained cardiomyopathy or arrhythmias in young adults
Early onset diabetes mellitus with iron overload
references: Pietrangelo A. Hereditary Hemochromatosis: Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Treatment. Gastroenterology. 2010.
Brissot P, et al. Hemochromatosis. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2018.
